text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ ۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ

words.gloss_range: opening vocative particle that summons the whole ayah into direct address
words.prose: {{ar:يَٰٓ}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens the ayah as direct summons before any proposition is stated, so the promise and prohibitions are heard by an addressed public rather than by detached observers. Its extended call creates a herald-like entry and prepares the collective audience named next. The placement before the assertion makes responsibility precede explanation.

topics.headline: direct-address opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by summoning hearers before presenting the truth claim.
topics.reason: The vocative particle sets direct-address scope over the following assertion and prohibitions.

topics.headline: collective summons range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call is not spatially narrow; it reaches the public human audience being formed.
topics.reason: The vocative force is locally discourse capture, not a claim about physical distance.

topics.headline: sustained call onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening sound lingering before the addressee is named.
topics.reason: The written and recited long call supports an audible public onset without changing syntax.

topics.headline: audience before assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accountability is staged before the premise and prohibitions unfold.
topics.reason: The vocative precedes the emphatic clause, making audience formation the first movement.

words.gloss_range: vocative support form that carries the call until the following appositive names the audience

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite human collective resolving the vocative support

words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ayyuhā}}) holds the vocative construction open until {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:al-nāsu}}) resolves who is being hailed. Its wider which-like openness is locally frozen into an address carrier, so the word gives the definite class address formal weight rather than leaving a bare call. Its alertive shape briefly delays the named audience, so the arrival of the human collective feels public and classified.

topics.headline: vocative support resolved by apposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the address is grammatically suspended until the next word names the audience.
topics.reason: The construction carries the vocative slot and licenses the following definite appositive.

topics.headline: open ayy fixed as address carrier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a wider which-like form is locally frozen into a formal summons.
topics.reason: The local vocative formula fixes the broader field as address support.

topics.headline: alertive fused address form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the form itself holding attention before the noun arrives.
topics.reason: The fused support plus alertive element prepares the following definite class noun.

topics.headline: delayed named audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase stages the audience rather than naming it instantly.
topics.reason: The two-part vocative delays the identifier and makes the next word the completion of the public call.

words.gloss_range: definite collective human addressee in nominative apposition
words.root_gloss_range: human sociality, familiarity, perception, and the contested forgetfulness derivation; locally a public human collective vulnerable to deception
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:al-nāsu}}) names the addressees as the definite human collective, not a subgroup and not the subject of the following assertion. Its nominative apposition completes the vocative frame, while the second-person suffixes later keep this same public audience inside both prohibitions. The social and perceptual root pressure makes the warning about shared human susceptibility to appearances; the same public-warning frame is also visible in 31:33.

topics.headline: definite appositional addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that humans are addressed before the proposition begins, not made the subject of the promise clause.
topics.reason: Case and attachment evidence identify the word as apposition to the vocative support.

topics.headline: social human collectivity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that deception is framed as a public human risk, not a private exception.
topics.reason: The root and noun choice support social/perceptual humanity while local grammar keeps the collective address primary.

topics.headline: definite plural collective shape
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that definiteness and collective form make the warning universal in scope.
topics.reason: The al-marked collective matches the later plural object suffixes.

topics.headline: public warning network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the address belongs to a wider public warning formula, especially the parallel frame in 31:33.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite same-surah recurrence and 31:33; these support formulaic public address without overriding the local apposition.

words.gloss_range: emphatic accusative-governing particle that stabilizes the promise clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: result particle turning the truth premise into prohibition

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) turns the next words into an emphatic nominal assertion: the promise is set as the governed topic and truth as its predicate. The particle answers possible heedlessness before the prohibitions arrive, making the later warnings rest on established reality. Its compact form controls the whole premise before {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns certainty into consequence.

topics.headline: emphatic nominal government
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices certainty being made visible through case government, not only through vocabulary.
topics.reason: The particle governs the accusative promise noun and predicate structure.

topics.headline: assertion against heedlessness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the premise addresses a listener who might neglect or resist the claim.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle supplies stance toward possible doubt while remaining a syntactic governor.

topics.headline: compact assertion control
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a small particle carrying the weight of the whole truth clause.
topics.reason: The form compresses emphasis and government before the longer warnings unfold.

topics.headline: premise before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah grounds prohibition in a truth premise rather than starting with command alone.
topics.reason: The emphatic nominal clause precedes and licenses the practical turn.

words.gloss_range: accusative verbal noun naming the divine promise as a present object of predication
words.root_gloss_range: promise, threat, pledged outcome, and appointed fulfillment; locally the binding divine commitment predicated as truth

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic particle governing the promise clause
proper divine name as source of the promise

words.prose: {{ar:وَعْدَ}} ({{tr:waʿda}}) is the governed verbal noun of {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}), so a future-facing commitment is made into the present topic of certainty. Its construct bond to {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) specifies the promise by source before truth is predicated, preventing it from sounding like impersonal fate. The root range can include promise, threat, and appointment; beside {{ar:حَقٌّ}} ({{tr:ḥaqqun}}), the local payoff is fixed fulfillment, with formulaic echoes including 4:122 and same-surah contrasts in 35:31 and 35:40.

topics.headline: verbal noun as governed premise member
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the promised future treated as a present grammatical entity that can be called true.
topics.reason: The word is the accusative ism of the emphatic particle and the head of the construct phrase.

topics.headline: pledged future as fixed appointment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise carries appointed fulfillment, not vague reassurance.
topics.reason: The root range survives as pledged outcome while the predicate selects the binding fulfillment side.

topics.headline: singular construct verbal noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a single source-bound commitment rather than plural or anonymous promises.
topics.reason: The articleless construct and verbal-noun form make the promise dependent on the divine name and stable for predication.

topics.headline: promise-truth formula as anti-deception premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that familiar promise-truth language, including 4:122, is turned here into practical resistance to deception.
topics.reason: The row family links the local promise-truth phrase with 4:122 and with 35:31 and 35:40, while the local clause remains primary.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as genitive source of the promise
words.root_gloss_range: worshipful orientation, refuge, awe, and the proper divine name; locally the singular source of the promise

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition that later governs the same divine name as deception domain

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) completes the construct as the promise source, so reliability is tied to the named divine referent before any deception clause appears. The proper name is not a generic sacred label; it anchors the premise in singular divine authority, and beside the truth predicate it makes divine reference and truth-status reinforce one another. Its recurrence later after {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) creates a role contrast: source of true promise here, domain exploited by deception at word 17.

topics.headline: genitive promise source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the promise is grammatically owned by the divine name before its truth is stated.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the divine name as genitive complement of the construct head.

topics.headline: proper divine authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that certainty rests on the singular worshiped referent, not on anonymous futurity.
topics.reason: The proper-name function is local; broader awe and refuge derivations support authority without replacing the name.

topics.headline: compact construct adjacency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the promise and divine name forming one tight dependency unit.
topics.reason: The adjacent genitive form and recited liaison keep the source relation compact.

topics.headline: same name, contrasting roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same divine name later shifting from truth-source to exploited domain, which protects God from being confused with the deceiver.
topics.reason: The local repetition between words 6 and 17 creates role contrast under different governors.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative predicate declaring the promise established truth and due reality
words.root_gloss_range: truth, reality, right, establishedness, and due claim; locally truth-status that grounds the prohibitions

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: result particle launched after the truth predicate

words.prose: {{ar:حَقٌّ}} ({{tr:ḥaqqun}}) closes the premise by naming the promise as established reality, not merely as an accurate report. The indefinite predicate gives qualitative force: the divine promise has truth-character and due claim. From this firm closure, {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) can turn certainty into the command not to be deceived.

topics.headline: indefinite predicate of certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the promise receiving a settled status in a nominal clause without an overt verb.
topics.reason: The word is nominative predicate of the emphatic clause.

topics.headline: truth and due reality converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised future is both true and binding, which weakens deceptive immediacy.
topics.reason: The root range joins fact, right, and due claim; the local predicate selects that convergence.

topics.headline: standing noun with firm closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices truth presented as a standing condition rather than a process becoming true.
topics.reason: The noun form, tanwin, and hard close support qualitative finality before the next particle.

topics.headline: truth premise to prohibition hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole double warning depends on this compact truth premise.
topics.reason: Rows link the predicate with the following consequence particle and with promise-truth parallels such as 4:122 and 35:31.

words.gloss_range: result particle that turns the premise into the first prohibition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first prohibitive negator fused after fa

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from truth to consequence. It makes the first prohibition follow from the claim that the divine promise is true, rather than reading as detached moral advice. Fused with the following {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), it delivers inference and negative command as one practical turn.

topics.headline: consequence from premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that resisting deception is grammatically inferred from the truth claim.
topics.reason: The particle links the emphatic premise to the first prohibitive clause as result.

topics.headline: sequence plus inference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the warning both follows after and follows from the premise.
topics.reason: The particle range supports sequence and consequence, both locally licensed by the clause boundary.

topics.headline: fused practical turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices consequence and prohibition arriving as one compact surface unit.
topics.reason: The proclitic form attaches directly to the prohibitive particle.

topics.headline: truth closure becomes command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah changing speech act at this particle.
topics.reason: The particle mediates the move from assertion to negative command.

words.gloss_range: first prohibitive negator governing the urgent deception verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive here, not merely descriptive negation. It bars the success of the coming deception event and makes the addressed humans responsible to resist what worldly life might do to them. As the first of two repeated negative particles, it starts a parallel warning frame that will be reopened at word 14.

topics.headline: prohibitive, not descriptive negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah commands prevention of deception rather than only reporting that deception is false.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following energetic imperfect as a negative command.

topics.headline: blocked event success
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the target is deception succeeding upon the audience.
topics.reason: The negator rejects the event as allowable within the first warning.

topics.headline: fa-la compression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices inference and prohibition compressed into one audible launch.
topics.reason: The fused sequence follows the consequence particle and opens the urgent command.

topics.headline: first half of repeated negative frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two distinct deception threats separated by repeated prohibition.
topics.reason: This first particle begins the pair that distinguishes worldly-life deception from deception concerning God.

words.gloss_range: first emphatic deception verb with the addressees as object and worldly life as delayed subject
words.root_gloss_range: deception, false security, hidden risk, and attractive surface over danger; locally the action worldly life must not be allowed to perform

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: delayed feminine subject of the first deception verb

words.prose: {{ar:تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ}} ({{tr:taghurrannakumu}}) places the audience inside the verb as object before the deceiving subject is named. The feminine agreement points ahead to {{ar:ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥayātu}}), while the heavy energetic ending makes the prohibition urgent. The gh-r-r field gives the warning a false-security and hidden-risk texture; variant readings can lighten the sound or pressure the agreement, but the local frame keeps the first warning centered on worldly life deceiving the addressees.

topics.headline: object first, delayed life-agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the danger striking the addressed audience before the agent is revealed.
topics.reason: The verb is a prohibitive energetic imperfect with second-person plural object suffix and feminine agreement with the delayed subject.

topics.headline: false security under hidden risk
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deception as unsafe confidence in attractive appearances, not only a false statement.
topics.reason: The gh-r-r root range supports concealed risk and delusive surface; the local subject will be worldly life.

topics.headline: energetic and variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the heavy ending pressing the warning, while accepted variants expose sound and agreement pressure without changing the local prohibition.
topics.reason: The heavy nūn, object suffix, and cited qiraat support urgency and form pressure while grammar preserves the life-agent parse.

topics.headline: first gh-r-r warning beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first verb beginning the ayah’s repeated deception chain.
topics.reason: The row family links this verb to the second verb and final noun, with 3:185 and 35:40 as deception-field echoes.

words.gloss_range: definite life noun functioning as delayed subject of the first deception verb
words.root_gloss_range: life, vitality, animation, reviving, and lived condition; locally the vivid life-world only as qualified by the near-world adjective
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥayātu}}) arrives after the verb as the subject that can deceive, so life is personified as an acting horizon. The word is not condemned as vitality in itself; its full local force depends on the following {{ar:ٱلدُّنْيَا}} ({{tr:al-dunyā}}), which narrows life into the near-world form. Same-surah life and revival echoes such as 35:9 and 35:22 make the warning sharper: one mode of life can mislead about fuller reality.

topics.headline: delayed feminine subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that life itself is grammatically made the agent of deception.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the noun as delayed nominative subject of the first verb.

topics.headline: vitality narrowed by worldliness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the problem is not life as such but vivid immediacy when qualified as near-worldly.
topics.reason: The root field of vitality survives, while the adjective restricts the local deceiving agent.

topics.headline: abstract life-system as agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an abstract verbal noun acting grammatically like a deceiver.
topics.reason: The definite feminine verbal noun can occupy the subject slot and accept the matching adjective.

topics.headline: life phrase completed by adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the agent phrase remains incomplete until the next word closes it.
topics.reason: Rows connect the delayed subject to the following adjective and to broader life contrasts including 29:64, 35:9, and 35:22.

words.gloss_range: definite feminine adjective specifying life as the near/lower worldly horizon
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, low-hanging reachability, and lower rank; locally the qualifier that makes life deceptive by immediacy

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: life noun modified by the near-world adjective

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلدُّنْيَا}} ({{tr:al-dunyā}}) closes the first agent phrase by making the deceiving life specifically the near and lower life. Its agreement with {{ar:ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥayātu}}) blocks a separate-agent reading and turns the two words into one specified horizon. The root’s nearness and lowness explain the mechanism: what is close and reachable can feel more real than the promised truth, a contrast also sharpened in 87:16-17.

topics.headline: adjective narrowing the subject phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices life being specified before the first warning clause closes.
topics.reason: Agreement and attachment evidence mark the word as an adjective modifying the life noun.

topics.headline: near-lower horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that deceptive power comes from proximity joined to lower rank.
topics.reason: The d-n-w range keeps nearness and lowness active in the local adjective.

topics.headline: feminine definite qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices morphology binding the adjective to life rather than creating a standalone world noun.
topics.reason: The al-marked feminine adjective agrees with the definite head.

topics.headline: first agent balanced with final deceiver
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a two-word life-horizon balanced against the final compact deceiver noun.
topics.reason: Rows relate the completed first agent phrase to later delusion language and to hereafter contrast in 87:16-17.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction adding a second prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the second warning without making it merely a causal restatement of the first. The first prohibition has closed, and this conjunction opens a coordinated parallel danger. Its small form carries the transition from worldly-life deception to deception concerning God while preserving one continuous address to the same audience.

topics.headline: coordination, not fresh inference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second prohibition added beside the first rather than derived from it by another result particle.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second prohibitive clause with the first.

topics.headline: additive escalation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relation is additive while the danger escalates in domain.
topics.reason: The conjunction leaves the relation open enough for parallelism and escalation.

topics.headline: minimal clause linker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a single letter joining two long warning clauses.
topics.reason: The short conjunction bears a full clause-linking load.

topics.headline: boundary between two threats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah keeping worldly enticement and God-related deception distinct.
topics.reason: The conjunction stands between repeated prohibitive frames and preserves the boundary between clauses.

words.gloss_range: second prohibitive negator reopening command scope for theological deception

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second energetic deception verb governed by the repeated prohibition

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is repeated instead of being left implicit, giving the second deception its own barred event. It governs {{ar:يَغُرَّنَّكُم}} ({{tr:yaghurrannakum}}) with the same urgent negative-command force as the first warning. The repetition keeps deception concerning God from being absorbed into the worldly-life clause.

topics.headline: fresh prohibitive scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second warning receiving its own negative-command force.
topics.reason: The repeated particle governs the second energetic verb.

topics.headline: barred God-related deception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misuse of divine reference is separately blocked, not treated as a side note.
topics.reason: The negation targets the success of deception attached to the following prepositional phrase.

topics.headline: wa-la visible fusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices coordination and prohibition arriving as one compact second launch.
topics.reason: The fused sequence marks the clause as both parallel and new.

topics.headline: two-beat negative frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired prohibitions as two distinct threat frames.
topics.reason: The repeated particle divides worldly-life deception from the final deceiver’s God-related deception and bridges into 35:6.

words.gloss_range: second emphatic deception verb taking the audience as object and routing deception through God-reference
words.root_gloss_range: deception and false security; locally repeated as a second verb whose domain is marked by the following bi phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional phrase routing deception through divine reference

words.prose: {{ar:يَغُرَّنَّكُم}} ({{tr:yaghurrannakum}}) repeats the urgent gh-r-r verb, but the masculine agreement and following {{ar:بِٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:bi-llāhi}}) move the deception into a new domain. The addressees again appear as object before the domain and final subject are revealed, so human vulnerability stays foregrounded. The matching sound with word 10 creates a refrain, while the changed complement makes this warning about false security concerning or by appeal to God; 31:33 preserves the same double-prohibition pattern.

topics.headline: second energetic verb with delayed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the addressees held as object before the domain and deceiver are named.
topics.reason: The verb is a prohibitive energetic imperfect with object suffix, bi complement, and delayed masculine subject.

topics.headline: same deception, new domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deception shifting from worldly-life appearances to false security attached to divine reference.
topics.reason: The gh-r-r field repeats, but the following prepositional phrase locally routes it through God-reference.

topics.headline: masculine prefix and repeated pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second verb sounding like the first while signaling a different subject.
topics.reason: The masculine prefix, suffix shape, gemination, and energetic ending create parallelism with shift.

topics.headline: paired verb refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one deception root recurring as the subjects and domains change.
topics.reason: Rows connect the paired verbs, final noun, and the same double-prohibition wording in 31:33.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the divine name as domain, means, cause, or invoked ground of deception

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine name governed by bi as deception domain

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the pivot that prevents the second clause from saying God deceives. It governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) as the domain or invoked ground through which deception works: about God, through God-talk, or by appeal to God’s name. Because it comes before the final deceiver, the threatened sacred domain is heard before the culprit is named.

topics.headline: prepositional complement frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices God-reference governed by a preposition, not functioning as deceiving agent or direct object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following divine name as prepositional complement of the verb.

topics.headline: domain and pretext range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the warning widening to deception about God and through God-talk while excluding an oath reading here.
topics.reason: The particle can mark sphere, means, cause, or pretext; local post-verbal position selects that relational range.

topics.headline: proclitic bond to divine name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition visibly and audibly fused to the divine name.
topics.reason: The proclitic form creates a compact governed unit.

topics.headline: prepositional pivot between repeated verbs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second gh-r-r verb redirected from worldly life to claims attached to God.
topics.reason: The particle differentiates the second prohibition and places the domain before the final subject.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name governed by bi as the domain exploited by deception
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship, refuge, and orientation associations; locally the fixed divine referent as governed domain, not deceiving agent

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the divine name in the second deception frame

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) returns under a different governor. Earlier it was the source of the true promise; here, after {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), the same proper name marks the domain that deception can exploit. The grammar protects the divine referent from agency misreading while exposing false confidence built around God-reference, precisely where worship, refuge, and deepest orientation should be secure; the fixed phrase also recurs in 31:33.

topics.headline: genitive after bi
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name as governed complement while humans remain the object of deception.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the divine name; it is not direct object or subject.

topics.headline: orientation field exploited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deception attacking the place where worship, refuge, and deepest orientation should be secure.
topics.reason: The proper name is local; broader orientation and refuge associations explain why misuse of this reference is serious.

topics.headline: same name, changed surface role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices morphology shifting the same name from construct possessor to prepositional complement.
topics.reason: The attached preposition changes the surface relation while the proper name remains stable.

topics.headline: truth-source versus deception-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah distinguishing divine reliability from claims made around God; 31:33 repeats the same God-related deception formula.
topics.reason: Rows connect word 6 and word 17 as same-name role contrast and cite 31:33 as a formulaic parallel.

words.gloss_range: definite final subject naming the deceiver or delusive force at the ayah close
words.root_gloss_range: deception, delusion, false security, vulnerability, and intensive deceiver/process; locally the final nominative subject of the second verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accepted variant foregrounding delusion itself as subject

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْغَرُورُ}} ({{tr:al-gharūru}}) finally names the delayed subject of the second verb, revealing the deceiving force after the object and God-related domain have already been heard. Its definite intensive noun form concentrates the gh-r-r action into an identifiable deceiver or delusive force that exploits unguarded susceptibility and the bright-surface danger of false security; the accepted {{ar:ٱلْغُرُورُ}} ({{tr:al-ghurūru}}) reading foregrounds delusion itself as agentive without changing the warning’s grammar. As the final word, it completes the triple gh-r-r chain from the two verbs to the closing culprit, with 35:6 specifying the enemy and 31:33 preserving the same eschatological caution.

topics.headline: delayed nominative culprit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word resolving the second clause by naming who performs the deception.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the noun as delayed nominative subject of the second verb.

topics.headline: intensive deceiver or delusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices delusion becoming an identifiable force that exploits human susceptibility and false security.
topics.reason: The gh-r-r range and qiraat evidence keep deceiver and delusion-process readings inside the same subject role.

topics.headline: definite final nominalization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deceptive action stabilized into a noun and made to linger at the close.
topics.reason: The definite intensive noun, variant vowel pattern, and final sound all support a climactic landing.

topics.headline: triple gh-r-r closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah escalating from two deception verbs to the named source of delusion, with 35:6 and 31:33 sharpening the frame.
topics.reason: Rows connect the two verbs and final noun, cite 35:6 for next-ayah specification, 31:33 for parallel warning, and 35:40 for false-promise recurrence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The promise noun at word 4 and certainty noun at word 6 stand before the near-life phrase at words 9-10 and the three occurrences of the deception root at words 8, 12, and 14.
baseline_models.mechanism: A speech-act opening future expectation is certified as fixed reality and obligation, while proximate life and a deceiving agent exert pressure through an attractive but unstable display. The contrast is temporal and evidential: what is nearest can feel most real without being the most reliable.

activation_trace.role: This branch contributes a spoken commitment that opens expectation, furnishing the future pole of the mechanism.
This branch contributes stable correspondence with reality, making the commitment more than hopeful speech.
This branch contributes nearness, assigning immediate experience the competing evidential advantage.
This branch contributes an attractive appearance that does not hold, making display the mechanism by which nearness overclaims reliability.

changed_reading.before: The ayah gives a general assurance followed by a warning against distraction.
changed_reading.after: The warning stages a contest between the felt evidence of the near present and the greater stability of a promised future; immediacy is persuasive but not probative.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same deception root governs two prohibitions: life is the first grammatical source, while an animate deceiver is the second; the divine name also recurs at words 5 and 13.
baseline_models.mechanism: Deception can arise from the structure of lived benefits and from an intentional persuader. Unknown outcome and inexperience explain why real goods can become risky without making life itself unreal, while the second channel can manipulate the hearer's relation to the worshiped one.

activation_trace.role: This branch contributes exposure to an unknown outcome, turning deception into mispriced consequence rather than mere false statement.
This branch contributes soft inexperience, supplying the human vulnerability through which both channels operate.
This branch contributes genuine benefit and good, allowing life to be useful while still becoming a misleading horizon.
This branch contributes the worship relation, so the second deception can corrupt trust and devotion rather than only appetite.

changed_reading.before: A single unspecified deceiver distracts people with worldly attractions.
changed_reading.after: Two readings coexist: life's real benefits can conceal their uncertain end, and an intentional persuader can weaponize that vulnerability, including through claims about God.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The promise root at word 4 has a dominant commitment inventory and a non-dominant mapped inventory of counting, preparation, and recurrent time; the near-life adjective at word 10 presses against that interval.
baseline_models.mechanism: The split root mapping permits a form-distant secondary model: fulfillment is not merely spoken but approached through counted duration and prepared readiness. Nearness then deceives by demanding closure before the accounted interval is complete.

activation_trace.role: This non-dominant branch contributes preparation for a coming event, giving the promise a readiness dimension.
This non-dominant branch contributes a counted waiting interval, supplying temporal structure to delayed fulfillment.
This non-dominant branch contributes marked and recurring time, suggesting an account rather than an indefinite postponement.
This branch contributes proximity, which the reader assigns as the pressure to judge before the count is complete.

changed_reading.before: The promise is a spoken commitment about an unspecified future.
changed_reading.after: Alongside the dominant speech-act reading, a secondary mapping makes it a future with counted preparation; the nearby present tempts premature verdicts about an unfinished schedule.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately following ayah supplies a rebellious adversary, repeated enmity, a verbal call, and faction formation. This sharpens the focus ayah's animate deceiver into a recruiter whose lure moves hearers from inclination to affiliation, without eliminating life's separate non-agentive pressure.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the unstable lure used by the recruiting agent.
This context branch contributes an actively rebellious agent, giving personal force to the second prohibition.
This context branch contributes explicit hostility, so the persuasive approach is adversarial rather than neutral advice.
This context branch contributes calling and verbal inclination, supplying the transition from lure to recruitment.
This context branch contributes a group organized around a view, making affiliation the recruiter's functional outcome.

structural_cues: 35:6 immediately follows the focus, repeats the enemy relation, and sequences adversary, call, party, and destination.
The focus itself assigns life and an animate deceiver to separate prohibitions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adversary, call, and faction; I infer a recruitment pipeline in which deceptive appearance enables affiliation. A live alternative is that 35:6 names only one instance of the deceiver while the first prohibition remains an environmental mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The animate deceiver is an unspecified source of misleading claims.
changed_reading.after: One strong reading sees deception as adversarial recruitment: words incline the hearer into a shared party, while worldly life remains a distinct channel rather than merely the agent's disguise.

context_deltas.mechanism: The ordered sequence in 35:8 moves from beautification of a bad deed to the actor seeing it as good. Deception therefore need not hide the object; it can reverse the evaluator's value assignment so that a known act appears commendable from within.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch contributes attractive instability, now sharpened as altered valuation rather than simple concealment.
This context branch contributes the active presentation of something as beautiful, initiating the evaluative reversal.
This context branch contributes actual badness, preserving the gap between the deed's condition and its appearance.
This context branch contributes inward judgment and reflection, locating the distortion in the actor's own appraisal.
This context branch contributes the positive pole opposed to badness, completing the reversal.

structural_cues: 35:8 presents a compact bad-deed to beautification to self-seeing-as-good chain.
The passive presentation and the actor's own seeing leave external suggestion and self-justification simultaneously live.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies beautification, badness, seeing, and goodness in sequence; I infer that deception recodes evaluation rather than merely withholding facts. The materially live alternative is whether the recoding is imposed by an external decorator or stabilized by the actor's self-reading.

changed_reading.before: Worldly deception makes a false object look attractive.
changed_reading.after: Deception can make one's own bad action read as good, so the warning targets a corrupted act of evaluation as much as an attractive external object.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus life's latent earth-renewal branch becomes explicit in 35:9, where dead land receives life and the sequence is likened to rising again. Life is therefore not intrinsically the false pole: its recurring material processes can disclose the promise, while treating near vitality as self-originating or final remains deceptive.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch carries a latent image of land becoming alive through rain, allowing life itself to bear evidential potential.
The focus branch contributes nearness, which distinguishes deceptive closure around present life from life as such.
This context occurrence realizes the same rain-and-earth branch, converting a latent focus image into an explicit material sequence.
This context branch contributes lifeless land and matter, furnishing the state that renewal reverses.
This context branch contributes revival after death, assigning the ecological reversal as an analogy for fulfillment.

structural_cues: 35:9 sequences wind, cloud, dead land, enlivening, and an explicit comparison to rising.
The focus makes near life a possible deceiver but does not call life false.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit material analogy between revived land and rising; I infer that worldly vitality can witness to the promise when read as recurrence rather than finality. A narrower alternative confines the analogy to resurrection and leaves the focus life's role wholly adversarial.

changed_reading.before: Worldly life stands only as the rival that distracts from the true promise.
changed_reading.after: Life is ambivalent: its nearness can close perception, yet its cycles of renewal can materially rehearse the promised reversal of death.

context_deltas.mechanism: Counted life extension and reduction are placed in an obligating record, celestial motion runs to a fixed limit, and accountability is delayed to a named term that eventually arrives. These cues activate the focus promise's non-dominant counting inventory: delay is structured and measured, not evidence of failure.

activation_trace.role: The focus's non-dominant branch contributes a counted interval, which context turns from a remote possibility into a coherent timing model.
This context branch contributes life extended through time, supplying the measured span within which apparent delay occurs.
This context branch contributes partial subtraction, making duration an account capable of measured decrement.
This context branch contributes a recorded determination with binding force, stabilizing the temporal account.
This context branch contributes a fixed temporal limit to celestial motion, broadening measured timing beyond an individual life.
This context branch contributes postponement to a later time, distinguishing deferral from cancellation.
This repeated context branch contributes both the appointed limit and its arrival, closing the measured interval.

structural_cues: 35:11 joins extended and reduced lifespan to a record; 35:13 joins motion to a named term; 35:45 joins delay to that term's arrival.
The focus places the certainty assertion before its warning against the pressure of the near present.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies counted lifespan, binding record, fixed limits, delay, and arrival; I infer that these unpack the promise's timing rather than form independent chronology. An alternative is that they establish creaturely limits generally without specifying the focus promise's schedule.

changed_reading.before: The promise is true eventually, but its delay is left as an empty gap.
changed_reading.after: The gap becomes an accounted interval: duration can increase or diminish, remains recorded, and ends at an appointed arrival, so non-immediacy does not imply non-fulfillment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated non-equivalence chain in 35:19-22 contrasts blindness and sight, darkness and light, and life and death. Read back into the focus, deception works by flattening consequential distinctions, while truth preserves fit between a thing's appearance, condition, and end.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch contributes correspondence with reality, supplying the criterion that distinguishes rather than equalizes.
The focus branch contributes unstable appearance, which can make opposed conditions seem exchangeable.
This context branch contributes comparison and equivalence, with the negated construction refusing to flatten the pair.
This context branch contributes loss of inward discernment, identifying a condition vulnerable to false equivalence.
This context branch contributes inward discernment, furnishing the opposed capacity to preserve distinctions.
This context branch contributes illumination, adding disclosed condition to the chain of non-equivalent poles.
This context branch contributes animate life, returning the focus life root inside an explicit non-equivalence.
This context branch contributes loss of life and force, supplying life's opposed end-state.

structural_cues: 35:19-22 repeats a negated equality construction across four paired contrasts and culminates in living and dead.
The focus juxtaposes stable truth with appearance-based deception before naming life as a possible source.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated categorical non-equivalence; I infer that resisting deception includes refusing substitutions that erase different ends. A live alternative is that the contrasts classify hearers only and do not directly define the mechanism of 35:5.

changed_reading.before: The warning asks the hearer simply to reject an attractive falsehood.
changed_reading.after: The warning also trains discrimination: present appearance and final condition are not equivalent, and deception succeeds when opposed trajectories are treated as interchangeable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence in 35:29-30 names hoped-for commerce that will not fail, then full payment and increase. This activates the focus deception root's unknown-outcome branch and recasts the true promise as guaranteed settlement: the contrast is between mispriced risk and a return whose payer completes and exceeds the account.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch contributes uncertain outcome and exposed risk, furnishing the failed-transaction side of the contrast.
The focus branch contributes a commitment that opens expectation, here functioning as the settlement guarantee.
This context branch contributes the heart's forward expectation, connecting commerce to the focus promise's hoped-for future.
This context branch contributes profit-seeking exchange, establishing the economic mechanism rather than a loose topic.
This context branch contributes stagnation that ends in ruin; its negation removes the trade's failure mode.
This context branch contributes completion without shortfall, supplying exact settlement of the account.
This context branch contributes compensation for work, identifying what is settled.
This context branch contributes growth beyond the completed amount, turning settlement into surplus rather than bare repayment.

structural_cues: 35:29-30 runs as expectation, commerce, negated failure, full payment, and increase.
The focus pairs a commitment certified as true with a deception branch explicitly involving unknown outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a continuous commercial and settlement sequence; I infer that it provides a counter-transaction to the focus's risk image. The live alternative is that commerce is only a reward metaphor and should not be pressed into a technical contract model.

changed_reading.before: The promise and deception contrast truth with false attraction in general terms.
changed_reading.after: The contrast can be read as risk allocation: worldly allure obscures its terminal loss, while the true promise underwrites a non-failing exchange completed in full and increased.

context_deltas.mechanism: In 35:40 the promise and deception roots are explicitly rejoined in a reciprocal human sequence: unjust parties promise one another only deception. The focus contrast therefore includes rival promise systems, one certified by stable reality and another sustained by mutual social repetition.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch contributes the authoritative commitment against which the context's exchanged commitments are measured.
The focus branch contributes stable reality, distinguishing authority from the number of people repeating a claim.
This context branch contributes exchanged commitments, making false assurance reciprocal rather than one-directional.
This context branch contributes parts of a larger group acting on one another, distributing the deception across a social network.
This context occurrence identifies the exchanged commitments as unstable lure, directly reconnecting the focus's warning to social speech.

structural_cues: 35:40 places the promise and deception roots in one restrictive clause with reciprocal participants.
This late echo does not erase 35:6's singular recruiter; it adds a distributed mechanism that can amplify the same lure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal promising and labels its remainder deception; I infer a socially circulated counter-promise that can feel credible through repetition. A narrower alternative limits this mechanism to the unjust partners addressed in 35:40 rather than every worldly deception.

changed_reading.before: The second deceiver is most naturally carried as a single external agent.
changed_reading.after: A competing reading remains live: deception is also socially distributed, as people mutually underwrite promises whose only backing is the lure they circulate.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context moves from the holding of the heavens and earth against displacement to bad plotting enclosing its own people and an established way that admits neither substitution nor redirection. This strengthens the focus truth as an invariant causal order: deceptive schemes do not escape consequence but curve back within it.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch contributes binding necessity, allowing truth to function as an operative order rather than only a correct proposition.
This context branch contributes active holding and restraint, furnishing cosmic stability as a material model.
This context branch contributes displacement from place or state, the instability that holding prevents.
This context branch contributes bad consequence descending and enclosing, supplying the return path of deceptive plotting.
This context branch contributes an established course repeatedly followed, turning self-return into patterned order.
This context branch contributes replacement of one thing by another; its negation denies substitution within the established course.
This context branch contributes change from one state to another; its negation denies diversion of the established course.

structural_cues: 35:41 gives a hold-versus-displacement relation; 35:43 repeats the bad-plotting construction and then twice negates alteration of the established way.
The plotting root's available branch inventory does not carry the plotted action cleanly, so that repeated construction is used only as a structural cue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies restraint, possible displacement, enclosing consequence, established course, and negated alteration; I infer that the plot's return manifests the same invariant order certified in the focus. A live alternative treats cosmic holding and moral self-return as adjacent but separate demonstrations.

changed_reading.before: The promise is true as a statement about a future result.
changed_reading.after: The promise can also be read as an already operative order: apparent manipulation cannot displace the governing course, and deceptive action remains enclosed by its own consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a concrete load-bearing maturity branch of the focus truth root through 35:11's bearing, birth, and lifespan sequence. It remains anchored to the certainty noun at word 6 and the promise at word 4, but downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for unfolding fulfillment, not as a replacement lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The certainty noun at word 6 has a branch of mature capacity, while the promise at word 4 has a branch of a sign that forecasts a coming condition.

activation_trace.role: This focus branch contributes maturity sufficient for bearing and use, furnishing the outlier's load-bearing image of truth.
This focus branch contributes a sign from which a coming state is anticipated, giving promise an incipient rather than merely verbal form.
This context branch contributes hidden inward bearing and fruit, supplying the gestational middle of the analogy.
This context branch contributes release of what was borne through birth, furnishing eventual disclosure.
This context branch contributes development across a life span, preventing the analogy from collapsing into instantaneous fulfillment.

changed_reading.before: Truth is static propositional correctness attached to a future commitment.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the promise is already present as a sign and hidden bearing whose truth reaches load-bearing maturity and eventual disclosure through measured time.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines three distant branches of the repeated deception root: a bright visible mark, the first edge of a thing, and incompletion. It remains anchored to all three focus occurrences and is sharpened by 35:8's bad-to-good appraisal sequence; downstream prose should label it an image-schema for premature judgment, not a dictionary sense imposed on the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated deception root at words 8, 12, and 14 stands beside the near-life adjective at word 10, permitting a model in which the nearest visible beginning is mistaken for the whole.

activation_trace.role: This focus branch contributes a conspicuous bright mark, furnishing the perceptual salience of the first visible surface.
This focus branch contributes the beginning of a thing, assigning the bright surface temporal priority.
This focus branch contributes shortfall and non-completion, marking what is omitted when the beginning is treated as the whole.
This focus branch contributes proximity, explaining why the visible first slice dominates attention.
This context branch contributes presentation as beautiful, showing how salience can be actively intensified.
This context branch contributes seeing, locating the truncated horizon in an act of perception.

changed_reading.before: Deception is a false claim laid over reality.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, deception is premature totalization: a bright and nearby first slice captures sight, while the incomplete and consequential remainder drops from the reading.

strongest_changes: 35:9 revises life from a simple rival into an ambivalent material witness whose renewal can rehearse the promised reversal.
35:40 directly opposes the true divine commitment to socially exchanged counter-promises whose only remainder is deception.
35:11, 35:13, and 35:45 activate a counted, recorded, and appointed interval, making delay structured rather than evidence of failure.
35:29-30 turns the promise-deception contrast into a coherent risk and settlement mechanism: unknown outcome versus non-failing, fully paid, increased return.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah sustained several non-collapsible mechanisms at once: temporal nearness, perceptual value reversal, adversarial recruitment, ecological recurrence, commercial settlement, social counter-promising, and invariant consequence. The threefold deception root and the split mapping of the promise root were especially productive without forcing one final identification of the deceiver.
remaining_uncertainties: The singular recruiter sharpened by 35:6 and the distributed social mechanism sharpened by 35:40 remain competing but compatible scopes.
The non-dominant counting mapping of the promise root is coherent with later timing cues but should remain explicitly exploratory.
The revived-land analogy may rehabilitate worldly life as evidence, or it may concern resurrection alone without revising life's role in the focus.
The link between cosmic stability and the self-return of bad plotting may express one invariant order or two adjacent demonstrations.

baseline.text: Ey insanlar, Allah'ın vaadi gerçektir. Dünya hayatı sizi aldatmasın; o aldatıcı da Allah hakkında sizi aldatmasın.

findings.text: Sabit ve vadesi belirli vaat, bugünün parlatılmış görünüşünün geleceğe ilişkin değerlendirmeyi bozmasına karşı bir ölçü oluşturur.
Dünya hayatının yakın ve aşağıda oluşu, en yakın katmanın bütün değer alanı sanılarak yukarı yönelen değerin görünmez kalması tehlikesini taşır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1 (35:1-14) Atmospheric Delivery and Vegetal Renewal
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A mobile atmospheric carrier delivers water that reverses terrestrial dormancy into growth and yield.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The resurrection analogy expands into fine-grained plant processes: water-laden cloud mass, returning green in dry herbage, bursting shoots, and tree growth after seasonal recession.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Dead ground returning to yield
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Unproductive ground receives rain, dry herbage greens again, tender shoots emerge, and the revived land produces a crop.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: soft fertile ground (quranic:root_000025:B002/m01); land's life through rain and vegetation (quranic:root_000383:B002/m01); dead unused land (quranic:root_001454:B003/m01); dry herbage revived by rain (quranic:root_001503:B004/m01); tender shoot emergence (quranic:root_000810:B004/m01); trees breaking into leaf and plants lengthening (quranic:root_000609:B017/m01); crop and tree yield (quranic:root_000043:B002/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Revival is staged as a causal sequence rather than a generic fertility image: dead ground, rain contact, regreening, shoot emergence, and edible yield. The result makes resurrection legible through the mechanics of seasonal plant return.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Generation proceeds through sexed bodies, an interior receptacle, gestational change, and eventual emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The human sequence is mirrored by a complete livestock scene of estrus, stallion display, threatened mounting, uncertain conception, and visible pregnancy.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Livestock courtship and uncertain conception
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A female desires mating, a stallion rises and bellows before mounting, and later signs either confirm pregnancy or disclose failed conception.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: female animal seeking the male (quranic:root_000248:B009/m01); stallion rising over females (quranic:root_000745:B003/m01); stallion's warning bellow before attack (quranic:root_001662:B005/m01); pregnancy becoming visibly apparent in ewe or camel (quranic:root_000531:B010/m01); suspected pregnancy that fails or is lost (quranic:root_000544:B013/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The lexical evidence forms a distinct animal reproductive sequence rather than an undifferentiated fertility theme. Display, threat, mating readiness, and uncertain gestation make generation vulnerable to failure as well as productive completion.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısındaki insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ve tek bir üyesini birlikte gösterir. Görünür olma açıklaması adlandırma gerekçesidir; insan olmanın kurucu tanımı değildir. Evde kimsenin bulunmadığını bildiren kalıp ise dal çekirdeğine genellenemez ve yalnızca kendi sözcüksel biriminde korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, insan türünü ve onun tekil ya da toplu üyelerini kapsar; yakınlık duygusunu, duyusal algıyı ve insana dönük yanı kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçimlerdeki insan ve insan topluluğu anlamı dal çekirdeğidir; evde hiç kimse bulunmadığını anlatan kalıp ayrı tutulur ve çekirdeğe yeni bir genel anlam katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında yer alan insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ya da tek bir üyesini belirtir. İnsanların görünür oluşu, bu adlandırma için aktarılan bir gerekçedir.

facets.statement: İnsan türünü, insanların oluşturduğu topluluğu veya bu türün tek bir üyesini görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında adlandırır.
Adlandırmanın insanların duyularla görünür oluşuna bağlanması, anlamın özü değil kökene ilişkin bir açıklamadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar, dalın insan türünü hem topluluk hem tek kişi olarak gösterebildiğinde ve görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfıyla karşıtlık kurduğunda birleşir. Görünürlük, ortak anlamdan çok adlandırmanın gerekçesi olarak sunulur.

concept_gloss.text: insan türü ve bu türden bir kişi
concept_gloss.applicability: İnsanları bir tür veya topluluk olarak anlatırken de bu türün tek bir üyesini belirtirken de kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan türü ile onun tekil üyesi arasındaki kapsamı ve temel sınıf karşıtlığını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Türün üyeleri topluca veya görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşıtı olarak anıldığında doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan türünün toplu olarak adlandırılmasını açık ve doğal biçimde korur.
